title: Fitness and Probity
summary: The standards of competence, honesty, integrity and financial soundness that directors must meet, how regulators act as gatekeepers at appointment, and how firms assess fitness on an ongoing basis.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The standards of competence, honesty, integrity and financial soundness that directors must meet, how regulators act as gatekeepers at appointment, and how firms assess fitness on an ongoing basis.
Learning Objectives: Apply fitness and probity standards to directors and other key roles
Prepare for a regulatory fitness and probity assessment or interview
Recognise the circumstances that call fitness or probity into question
Syllabus: Competent and capable: qualifications, experience, competence and capacity
Honest, ethical and acting with integrity, including non-financial misconduct
Financial soundness and the firm's due diligence and certification
Regulatory gatekeeping, interviews, refusals and lessons from case law
Intended Audience: Chairs, executive, non-executive and independent directors of regulated firms, fund boards and management companies
Senior managers preparing for a first board appointment or moving from an executive to a non-executive role
Company secretaries, heads of governance and compliance staff who support the board and its committees
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No prior governance training is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Examination of Governance for Collective Investment Schemes (2006–2007)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
Olivier Sibony, You're About to Make a Terrible Mistake! How Biases Distort Decision-Making (2020)
